report_name: Identity Attacks Drive Most Ransomware: Sophos Report

threat_actors.name: Ransomware Operators
threat_actors.description: A general class of financially-motivated threat actors responsible for ransomware incidents, as described in the 2026 Sophos State of Ransomware report. This entry represents the aggregate actor whose TTPs are analyzed in the report, focusing on identity-based attacks to bypass MFA.

attack_patterns.name: Spearphishing Attachment
attack_patterns.description: Malicious email with attachments was identified as a leading initial access vector in 26% of ransomware incidents.

attack_patterns.name: Spearphishing Link
attack_patterns.description: Phishing with malicious links was identified as a leading initial access vector in 24% of ransomware incidents.

attack_patterns.name: Valid Accounts
attack_patterns.description: Compromised credentials were used as the initial access vector in 23% of ransomware incidents.

attack_patterns.name: Multi-Factor Authentication Request Generation
attack_patterns.description: Attackers bypass MFA through MFA Fatigue or Push-Bombing, where they repeatedly send MFA push notifications to a user, hoping for an accidental or frustrated approval.

attack_patterns.name: Adversary-in-the-Middle
attack_patterns.description: Sophisticated phishing kits are used to create a proxy between the victim and a real login page to intercept credentials and MFA codes, ultimately to steal the session cookie.

attack_patterns.name: Steal Web Session Cookie
attack_patterns.description: After a successful Adversary-in-the-Middle (AiTM) phishing attack, the attacker captures the session cookie, which allows them to bypass MFA entirely and access the user's session.

attack_patterns.name: Multi-Factor Authentication Interception
attack_patterns.description: Attackers use SIM swapping, where they convince a mobile carrier to transfer a victim's phone number to an attacker-controlled SIM card, to intercept SMS-based MFA codes.

attack_patterns.name: Account Manipulation
attack_patterns.description: An attacker who gains access to an account may try to register their own device for MFA to establish persistence.

infrastructure.name: Adversary-in-the-Middle Phishing Infrastructure
infrastructure.description: Sophisticated phishing kits used to create a proxy between the victim and a real login page to capture credentials and session cookies, enabling MFA bypass.

indicators.name: Potential MFA Fatigue Attack via Azure AD
indicators.pattern:
title: Potential MFA Fatigue Attack via Azure AD
id: 2b9a1c8d-4e5f-4a9b-8c7d-6e5f4a3b2c1d
status: experimental
description: Detects Azure AD sign-in failures with error code 500121, which indicates the user denied an MFA prompt. A high volume of these events for a single user can indicate an MFA Fatigue (push-bombing) attack.
references:
  - https://cybermagazine.com/news/sophos-state-of-ransomware-report-a-step-ahead-of-attackers
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-07-17
tags:
  - attack.t1621
level: medium
logsource:
  product: azure
  service: signinlogs
detection:
  selection:
    ResultType: '500121'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects Azure AD sign-in failures with error code 500121. A high volume of these events for a single user can indicate an MFA Fatigue (push-bombing) attack, as described in the Sophos 2026 report.

indicators.name: New MFA Device Registration in Azure AD
indicators.pattern:
title: New MFA Device Registration in Azure AD
id: 8d7c6b5a-4e3f-4a2b-8c1d-9e8f7a6b5c4d
status: experimental
description: Detects the registration of new MFA security information for a user account in Azure AD. While often legitimate, this can also indicate an attacker who has compromised an account is attempting to establish persistence for MFA.
references:
  - https://cybermagazine.com/news/sophos-state-of-ransomware-report-a-step-ahead-of-attackers
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-07-17
tags:
  - attack.t1098
level: low
logsource:
  product: azure
  service: auditlogs
detection:
  selection:
    OperationName|contains:
      - 'User registered security info'
      - 'User registered authentication method'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects the registration of a new MFA device for a user account in Azure AD. The Sophos 2026 report notes that attackers who gain access may try to register their own device for MFA.
